threads.title: WHAT GIVES? — Squad Power, Matchmaking, Bots, and Division Advancement

original_post.text:
I would like to raise some questions about matchmaking, Squad Power, bot

participation, and division advancement in Mech Arena.

My intention is not to complain simply because I lose matches. Losing is part of

any competitive game. My concern is whether the matchmaking system consistently

produces balanced and enjoyable matches, and whether certain aspects of the

system make advancement unnecessarily difficult for some players.

I have been at essentially the same level, (Division 4), since the end of April

or beginning of May 2026. That means I have been experiencing this situation

for at least six months. I understand that advancement becomes more difficult

as players progress, but I would like to understand whether what I am experiencing

is simply the natural result of reaching my competitive level or whether other

matchmaking factors are influencing my results.

1. Bots and Match Composition

I have no objection to bots being used to fill out teams. I understand that they

can reduce waiting times and help ensure that matches begin without unnecessary

delays.

However, I believe bots should be complementary to the match and to the actual players

participating in it. They should help create a reasonably balanced team

environment, rather than become a source of imbalance.

Ideally, bots should be selected and assigned in a way that considers the capabilities

of the actual players on both teams. A bot should contribute to the match, not

become a liability that another player must constantly compensate for.

I recognize that no matchmaking system can guarantee perfectly balanced teams.

There will always be differences in player ability, equipment, tactics, and

performance. Nevertheless, there is a difference between an unpredictable match

and one in which the team composition appears to place one side at a

substantial disadvantage before the match even begins.

I would appreciate clarification on how bots are selected, how their capabilities

are determined, and whether their assignment takes the composition and

capabilities of the human players into consideration.

 2. Squad Power and Matchmaking

Plarium has previously stated that matchmaking considers multiple factors, including:

· Squad Power;

· Current online population in the player's region;

· Player skills;

· Other factors.

I understand that Squad Power is not necessarily the only consideration. However,

I would like clarification on precisely what is being measured.

For example:

· Does matchmaking consider only the active hangar, or does it also consider the

player's other hangars?

· Does it consider the player's total inventory or overall account progression?

· Does historical performance influence matchmaking?

· Are tournament results or performance in other game modes considered?

· Does the system adjust matchmaking based on recent win/loss records or winning

streaks?

I am not suggesting that any of these factors are necessarily being used. I am

asking because understanding which factors matter would help players understand

why they are being matched against particular opponents.

 3. My Statistics and Matchmaking Experience

My current overall statistics are:

· Battles: 3,543

· Wins: 1,637

· Kills: 22,605

· Win rate: 46.20%

· Kills per battle: 6.38

· Squad Power: 66,980

Because tournament battles are included in my overall statistics, separating the two

gives a more useful picture.

Standard matches

· Battles: 2,432

· Wins: 1,008

· Kills: 14,105

· Win rate: 41.45%

· Killsper battle: 5.80

Tournament matches

· Battles: 1,111

· Wins: 629

· Kills: 8,500

· Win rate: 56.62%

· Kills per battle: 7.65

I recognize that these are different game modes, with different opponents and

potentially different team compositions. Therefore, I am not claiming that the

difference proves a matchmaking problem. However, I do believe it raises a

reasonable question about how matchmaking operates across the different modes.

 I have also experimented with a substantially lower-powered hangar. In one test,

I assembled a hangar with approximately 4,000 Squad Power, using 16-energy

mechs and Rare pilots. The first six matches resulted in four wins and two

losses. After that, I experienced a prolonged losing streak.

This is only one personal observation, and I recognize that six matches are not

enough to establish a pattern or prove anything about the matchmaking

algorithm. Nevertheless, it is one reason I would like to understand whether

the game considers only the active hangar or other aspects of the account when

creating matches.

4. Recent Match Logs

I have also retained screenshots of my battle logs covering three days, from the

end of October into the beginning of November 2026.

The in-game logs retain only approximately 20 matches at a time, so I took multiple

screenshots to capture a larger portion of the match history.

I have transcribed 21 matches from those screenshots below. These are not

intended to be a definitive statistical study, nor do I suggest that three days

of results prove that the matchmaking system is biased. However, I believe they

may be indicative of the experience I have been describing.

I consider the MVP results worth mentioning because they show that I was still

able to perform well individually in at least some of these matches, including

matches that ended in defeat.

Again, I am not presenting these logs as proof of deliberate matchmaking manipulation.

They are a limited sample. However, I believe they provide a useful starting

point for examining team composition, bot participation, and the consistency of

matchmaking.

 I can provide the screenshots if they would be helpful.

5. A Player Should Be Allowed to Find Their Plateau

I believe every player should be allowed to find their own plateau.

By plateau, I mean the point at which a player begins to win and lose at

approximately the same rate. They have reached a level where the competition is

challenging, where victories must be earned, and where defeats are simply part

of the experience.

I do not necessarily consider that a bad thing. In fact, I think that is where the

real fun begins.

Once a player reaches that point, they can stop worrying quite so much about

advancement and start experimenting.

Maybe they decide to build a hangar consisting entirely of the fastest mechs

available, equipped with heavy weapons. Perhaps they want to build a hangar of

heavily armored tank mechs carrying beam and missile weapons. Maybe they want

to try a completely unconventional combination simply because it sounds

entertaining.

They can experiment with different weapons, pilots, implants, and mech combinations.

They can try strategies that might not be considered competitive or optimal,

simply to see whether they work. They can play for the enjoyment of the game

rather than constantly worrying about whether the next match will move them

forward or push them backward.

That is part of what makes a game enjoyable: having the freedom to experiment,

develop your own play style, and occasionally do something just because it is

fun.

There is nothing wrong with competition, and there is nothing wrong with wanting to

reach a higher division. But I believe the game should also reward players with

an enjoyable experience once they reach their natural competitive level.

 A player should be able to say, "I've found my level. Now let's have some

fun."

6. Division Advancement and Long-Term Enjoyment

I have been progressing through the tournament divisions, and I understand that

the competition becomes more difficult as a player advances. I expect that.

Stronger opponents should present a greater challenge, and I do not expect to

win every match.

However, I have been stuck at essentially the same level for at least six months, since

late April or early May. I find that frustrating because I believe I am capable

of progressing farther.

I am not asking for the game to make advancement easy, nor am I asking to be placed

against weaker opponents simply so that I can win more matches.

I am asking whether the matchmaking system provides a reasonable opportunity for

players to advance based on their performance, or whether other account-related

factors can make advancement increasingly difficult.

If the result is that I remain at my current level, I can live with that. I can

continue playing tournaments, log in when I want to compete, and use the time

between tournaments to improve my hangars whenever I have the resources to do

so.

That is not necessarily a bad way to enjoy the game.

But I would prefer that this be the result of fair competition rather than an

experience in which advancement feels unnecessarily restricted or inconsistent.

7. Why This Matters to Me

I want to make one thing clear: I genuinely enjoy Mech Arena.

 In fact, this is the only video game I play, and the only one I have continued to

play and enjoy since SimCity 2000, (yes, I am THAT old).

I am not someone who jumps from one game to another, nor am I looking for a reason

to stop playing. I enjoy the game, I enjoy building and improving my hangars,

and I enjoy competing.

That is precisely why this situation is frustrating.

I know I can go farther. I am not expecting to win every match, but I do expect

to have a reasonable opportunity to compete and advance. When I remain at

essentially the same level for six months, despite continuing to play and

improve my equipment, it naturally raises questions.

I would much rather spend my time experimenting with new hangar combinations,

trying different weapons, and enjoying the game than wondering whether the

matchmaking system is placing me at a disadvantage.

I want to keep playing. I simply want to understand what is happening.

8. Questions for Plarium

I would appreciate clarification on the following:

 1) Does matchmaking use the active hangar's Squad Power, the combined power of all hangars, or overall

inventory strength?

2) What does Plarium mean by player "skills," and how are they measured?

3) Does historical performance, tournament performance, or recent win/loss history influence matchmaking?

4) How are bots assigned to teams, and does the system attempt to balance their capabilities against the

actual human players?

5) Does matchmaking change when a player enters a new tournament division or approaches a division promotion?

6) Is there a mechanism that adjusts matchmaking based on a player's account progression, rather than the

equipment currently being used?

7) Does the system recognize when a player has been at essentially the same competitive level for an extended

period, and if so, how does that affect matchmaking?

I am not asking for the exact matchmaking formula or for preferential treatment. I am asking for enough transparency to understand how the system works and what factors influence the matches we receive.

I enjoy Mech Arena, and I want to continue enjoying it. I do not expect to win every match, nor do I expect the game to make advancement easy.

I simply want to know that the competition is reasonably balanced, that bots contribute positively to the experience, and that players are given a fair opportunity to find their level, advance when their performance warrants it, and enjoy the game once they get there.

Thank you for taking the time to consider the questions.

May you have a Great day.

Based on your feedback and our analysis of the last rebalance, we've decided to continue making further tweaks to improve Mech Arena. You can expect the next iteration of changes to go live on December 3.

Our core goal remains the same: we're aiming to improve underperforming Mechs and Weapons, while toning down some overly strong content.

📆 When?

The upcoming stage of the rebalance will be released 14 days from today, on December 3.

🔄 What?

This time, we're buffing the following content:

• Onyx: Ability now applies an EMP effect for 2s. Ability Damage has been increased by ~29%. Lastly, the lower the target's HP, the more Bonus Damage the Ability deals (up to x1.8 against targets at 20% HP or less).

Dev Note: For quite a long time, Onyx was falling behind more powerful Legendary Mechs. So we asked ourselves: how can we make it compete with the most powerful content?

The solution came pretty fast. We decided to make Onyx tougher and more threatening.

• From now on, Onyx's Ability will apply a short EMP effect to the enemy target, giving this Mech both survivability and Damage potential. A long-range stun opens up several new ways to use the Ability.

• Plus, we're introducing a new mechanic: the less HP the target has, the more Damage Onyx's Ability will deal.

We're super excited to hear what you guys think, because for us it's definitely a new way to play the Mech! <3

• Scorpius: Ability charges increased (1 → 2): Scorpius can now use its Ability twice before it goes on Cooldown. Ability Damage increased (x5). Increased Damage to Shields: the Ability deals x4 Damage to Personal Mech Shields and Mod Shields. Ability Range increased (75m → 90m), Ability Cooldown increased (7s → 10s).

Dev Note: Changing Scorpius was one of the hardest tasks for us. Whatever we tried just didn't feel like enough. But we believe we've finally found a way to make Scorpius a useful and threatening Attacker.

We actually did three things:

• We increased the Ability Damage.

• We added a Shield Damage coefficient, which means Scorpius will be very effective against Mod Shields and Personal Mech Shields.

• We added a second Ability charge, so Scorpius can now use its Ability twice before it goes on Cooldown.

The Damage increase is significant and it allows Scorpius to pose a large threat on the battlefield.

• Biform: Ally and self-healing per second increased by 200%. Ability Damage increased by 70%. Ability Cooldown reduced (14s → 12s). Ability Duration shortened (7s → 4s), and additional Ability Duration shortened (3s → 2s), so heals land faster.

Dev Note: Our newest Legendary healer felt powerful but we thought that might not be enough to really show the potential of this hard-to-get Mech.

So we increased both its healing and Damage capabilities. With this buff, it will be nearly impossible to kill a Mech while Biform is healing it!

• Blast RPGs: Damage per shot increased by 19.8%. Now applies the Weaken effect for 2s, effectively increasing Damage per magazine by 73.7%.

Dev Note: The concept of this Weapon started with a simple idea: "let's make Legendary RPGs".

But looking at the current state of the meta, we understood that it wasn't enough and we needed to buff these Weapons.

We increased the Damage, and we also added the Weaken effect, which makes its targets even more vulnerable.

• Chain Guns: Damage doubled. Kills and assists keep the barrel spinning and halve the Weapon's Reload Time until the next spin up.

Dev Note: This Weapon has a pretty interesting mechanic. However, it wasn't always easy to use, and the Damage left a lot to be desired. So we thought: why not play around with these things?

We drastically increased the Damage and also made the Weapon's main mechanic much easier to benefit from. Now, if you get a kill or an assist with this Weapon:

• You won't need to spin up the barrel again.

• Your Reload Time will be halved.

A nice bonus for playing aggressively, right? ;)

The following content will be nerfed to keep it fun and effective, but less dominant:

• Outlaw: Ability Range reduced (100m → 60m). The time that it takes for the Ability to come into effect has been adjusted to the new range: the maximum time of 2s now kicks in from 41m instead of 91m.

Dev Note: Outlaw has been dominating the battlefield for quite some time now. We actually like everything about this Mech, but its range seems a little too overpowered.

So the only thing we're changing is shortening the Ability Range. Outlaw players will need to be more careful and tactical.

• Geminis: Reload Time increased (6s → 8s).

Dev Note: Geminis are great Weapons. Their only downside is that it's simply too easy to benefit from them, and they deal a lot of Damage.

So we're slightly increasing the Weapon's Reload Time to make it a little less "spammy".

➡ ️ What's next after this rebalance?

As always, we'll continue monitoring the results of these changes, and we look forward to hearing your feedback.

original_post.text:
To begin, I don't mean to encourage people to quit. Nor to cause an immediate massive disruption in the player base. I just wanted to share my thoughts about plarium and the mech arena team's communications.

Every time there's a complaint about matchmaking the response is "we're constantly working on the matchmaking making gradual improvements, we hope you see an improvement soon" or whatever. Press them with more questions like "when exactly could we expect to see improvement?" or "what are you actually doing to make the matchmaking experience better"? They answered the former question once, the latter never. And most of the time if you wait long enough and can appear to improve a bit for a short few days, before refore rebounding back and ending up WORSE than the matchmaking we complained about. I made this complaint before that we often got improvements but they never lasted and the team I guess noticed it because I finally got to experience about a month of decent matchmaking.

After that, it's just been the same patters. "Please be patient [blah blah blah]". Ask the questions "when exactly can we expect to see improvements in the matchmaking?" and "what are you actually doing to improve the matchmaking experience?" No answers.

Then there's gear hub releases. Plarium as far as I know doesn't have a strict timeline for gear hub releases. They just arbitrarily decide when to release what equipment. And at least up until recently popular stuff took longer to make it to gear hub. So I inquired about it. Staff freaking lied to all our faces and said the opposite was true. Only just recently has what they say and what they do been aligned in that department. But for the longest time it was a complete lie. (Now watch me get banned for accusing staff of lying even though they 100% factually were)

And we all saw what happened with voidghost. Most generous interpretation of the situation is we can take them at their word there was a genuine breakdown in communication within the mech arena team, causing a failure to properly communicate with players what their actions regarding voidghost would be. And I don't think anyone who's been paying attention really believes the generous interpretation to be true. But yet I don't think it's because this exact situation happened before. No most people just mentioned it was really conspicuous the timing of the NERF and everything. Most players seem to have forgotten already this type of thing happened before, with burrow beams. Burrow beams released as just a completely overpowered weapon. We're talking about a medium ranged weapon that killed faster than close quarters weaponry that could also tunnel through mechs and mod shields and deal full damage to every target. Only later did they tell us it was an unintended mechanic but at least it was well before they NERFed it as opposed to using it as an excuse after NERFing it like with voidghost.

Ironically though that's the only thing that makes me think the lack of communication in regards to the voidghost NERF was just a genuine failure. Because they happened to communicate the NERF of burrow beams ahead of time. Everyone knew they were going to be NERFed so the vast majority accepted it even though I don't think anyone accepted their reasoning that burrow beams weren't meant to totally bypass shields. But it's also another reason I have a hard time believing them. Because what I think actually happened there with voidghost is it came out and immediately a bunch of people said "what the hell do you mean this thing can damage me while I can't damage it in return" and internally the team went "crap, we messed up again and made a totally overpowered piece of equipment that our players hate. We gotta NERF it. But we don't gotta tell them about it this time. They accepted the quick burrow beams NERF. And uh, there's no reason to sully the idea of purchasing it while the crate rush is ongoing so at least don't tell them while it is."

This is why I can't trust plarium. They said that their failure to communicate ab the voidghost NERF was an honest mistake and not up to their internal communication standards. I wasn't aware they had any. Poor communication is the norm here and I've made that complaint numerous times. I just refuse to believe it's not deliberate at this point. They're saying they'll do better communicating plans for NERFs next time. I say they need to improve their communication all around. And I think perhaps at least one person needs to be fired. Most likely from upper management because being real I know in the vast majority of cases these problems come from the top down.

I gotta also remind yall that nothing is perfect. Also stay positive and do not complain too much cuz that lets negative energy take you over so stay grateful for any acoins or credits you get, personally it just helps me and it might help you too.

Stay happy and make sure to follow discipline

threads.title: I still get to debate if Voidghost is broken, yay!

original_post.text:
Isn't it great when 90% of the talk about the game is whether or not certain mechs or weapons are OP? Just a good chunk of players not having fun playing against a mech or weapon that for many is stupid in concept. Then on the other side of that is players (often who have the mech or weapon in question by the way) saying it's not that bad and you just need to learn to counter it. I was worried plarium had settled the debate on voidghost early. But now the debate can continue.

Cause plarium is like "It was an unintended mechanic. That's why the damage boost remains active and ability to heals during the second immaterial phase. Totally unintended. You were absolutely never meant to figure out some weapons would keep firing while voidghost was immaterial. But since we just so happened to not communicate that it was totally an unintended mechanic the entire time the crate rush was running, which wasn't up to our communication standards (totally not planned), and everyone called us out on it we've decided to revert our NERF at least for the time being."

Thing is I'd already lost interest in the debate. As always, numbers should tell the story of whether or not it's overpowered. Theoretically I think it is. And regardless I don't like it. We've already got seeker and deathwalker which can be invulnerable and shoot at you while they're teleporting. I never liked them. Now we've got a mech that can do that, and doesn't need to be teleporting, doesn't need to be backtracking. And it can heal itself. Best idea to counter it I think would be something that can EMP it or catch it between abilities and prevent it from using again. This is derived from Terminator's advice. Oh yeah the advice also said to let it kill you then chase after it with a counter. And there's where my problem is.

Voidghost is a scout mech. A kind of mech designed for taking out important targets. Sometimes voidghost only needs to make 1 kill to do its job. And theoretically it's the perfect scout. You can make your way towards a targeted enemy even behind enemy lines risk free because of invulnerability. Start shooting your burrow beams or your storm racks and then go invulnerable again. Your target dies, you get some health back and you can move out of there risk free again because of being immaterial. When the NERF was applied I saw Terminator mentioned they were using savant. And then later watched a video by Mayer where he tried savant. This weapon is dumb with voidghost because of the fast flying rockets and quick magazine dump you can have the recast time up for a fraction of a second to use that weapon and go immaterial again. Very little risk to ones self while being able to deal a massive amount of damage to enemies, and that was after the NERF. I've had this idea that repeaters would work well with it since their magazines gradually refill. My idea is you would go immaterial to get into point blank range and dump repeaters into them and then if you couldn't finish them off if they still have a good bit of HP left go immaterial again and wait for the repeaters to reload a bit and then finish them off. Or do the opposite say you're pre ability you shoot them with your repeaters but you need to finish them off. Go immaterial and then finish them during recast time and get any health you might have lost back and then recast and escape back to safety.

To me, yeah still unreasonably efficient at what it's supposed to do. And it's definitely still going to be replacing certain things in their roles. But again, it's out. They released it as is. Even if the team isn't lying and those weapons continuing to fire while voidghost is immaterial was unintended they should have either communicated that sooner or pushed back the release of voidghost until they fixed it. But since things have gone the way they have they might as well leave it as is and let the numbers tell the story of whether or not it's broken.

Im making this just to share my opinion on how everybody in this forum is just pooping all over how bad the matchmaking is on Tournaments.

So i started returning to the game in April 2026, i had Sentinel, Gatecrasher4star, orion, killshot, & zephyr (i know i get a lot of burn outs from this game) LAST TIME i played was when Revokers were overpowered. Now returning and taking a peek to see if the game has gotten any better! I played the new Tournament. threads.title: Criticism and suggestions for the game.

original_post.text:
Well, I've praised the developers, now I can criticize them.

And the first thing I'd like to ask is: what is the connection between the "free-for-all" game mode and the tournament?

In the tournament, a player must demonstrate their skills and strengths, their mastery of the robot and its abilities, their understanding of the battlefield situation, and their capacity for teamwork. None of this applies to the "free-for-all" mode. In this mode, a great deal depends on chance, with the probability of such random factors coming into play being around 40%. These factors include the player's and the opponent's drop locations, as well as the player's respawn point—which often appears right behind their back.

All of this makes the inclusion of this game mod absolutely unacceptable for the tournament.

Please make "Free-for-All" a separate game mode.

The second point concerns player selection—a topic that is frequently discussed and often criticized.

I don't know the principles behind the matchmaking mechanism, but I would like the matchmaking criteria to include the following variables.

1. Win-loss ratio. 2. Number of battles fought. 3. Strongest team. 4. Robot tier (Rare, Epic, Legendary, etc.). And the search for an opponent team must proceed in precisely this order.

This is undoubtedly just my opinion, and I could, of course, be mistaken or under a misconception.

Another idea is to remove the 5v5 mode from the tournament and replace it with 3v3 and one-on-one modes. There is already plenty of 5v5 gameplay in the game. In this case, the number of battles must be four in one mode and four in the other.

And finally, don't hesitate to launch a 5v5 test mode where you can try out various matchmaking configurations. I am confident that players will participate in this mode, actively cooperate with you, and provide their feedback.

Best regards, Alex Sweetfire.
